sentences.text: Muyelensaurus was a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Late Cretaceous. Unlike many of its relatives, this animal had a more slender body build.
The known fossil remains include the base of the skull, vertebrae from the neck, back, and tail, as well as numerous limb bones.

A unique feature of its skull is that the basal tuber has a divergence angle of a right angle. Other distinctive traits include a concave thin lamina uniting the basal tuberosities and posterior dorsal neural spines with long pre-spinal laminae.

The genus Muyelensaurus was named in 2007 by paleontologists Jorge Calvo, Bernardo González Riga, and Juan Porfiri. The fossils were discovered by Jorge Calvo at Loma Lindero in Rincón de los Sauces, Neuquén, Argentina.
Originally assigned to the Portezuelo Formation, the remains were later reclassified to the Plottier Formation.
Some studies place Muyelensaurus as a basal member of the Lithostrotia, while other research positions it within the clade Rinconsauria.
A cladistic analysis placed Muyelensaurus pecheni and Rinconsaurus caudamirus in a new group within the Lithostrotia called Rinconsauria.

Estimates for the animal's age vary; some sources place it at approximately 89 million years ago between the Turonian and Coniacian stages, while others suggest it lived from the Coniacian to the Santonian, between 89.8 and 83.6 million years ago.

Recent research suggests that fossil material previously attributed to Muyelensaurus pecheni may belong to sauropods from more than one taxon, potentially restricting the species to the holotype specimen only.
